The triangle A, B, C has the most nodes but weighs only 1 + 2 + 1 = 4; the edge B to D, in the accent color, weighs 2 + 5 = 7. The card shows the result [B, D] with weight 7." width="100%"} With node weights (values, scores, sizes), the maximum-weight clique is the most valuable group of mutually connected nodes: the highest-scoring set of compatible features, the most valuable group of mutually compatible items or people, or the best consistent set of matches in structure alignment. Without weights it is a maximum clique, like `maximum_clique()`. Parallel edges count once and self-loops are ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_weight_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of a node attribute holding non-negative weights. If `None` (default), every node weighs 1. Every node must have the attribute. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[int], int | float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The clique's node IDs (sorted) and its total weight (`int` when unweighted). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, or a weight is missing, negative or not a number. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Branch and bound: candidates are colored greedily (heaviest first), and since a clique uses at most one node of each color class, the sum of the heaviest weight in each class bounds what the candidates can add (in the spirit of Kumlander, 2004, and Tavares et al.). The problem is NP-hard, but the bound prunes well on sparse graphs. The weight found matches NetworkX's `max_weight_clique`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The triangle A-B-C has three nodes, but B-D is heavier: ::: {#d509e06b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes( [("A", {"w": 1}), ("B", {"w": 2}), ("C", {"w": 1}), ("D", {"w": 5})] ) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("B", "D")]) nodes, weight = g.maximum_weight_clique(node_weight_attr="w") [g.get_label_from_id(n) for n in nodes], weight ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['B', 'D'], 7) ``` ::: :::
